rows.label: Subsequent events and pro forma net debt — paragraph 1
Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

The issuer states only Adjusted EBITDA and no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is derived from net income, income taxes, net interest and depreciation and amortization; every leverage and cover figure depends on that derivation, and the issuer-adjusted ratios are shown beside each one. Severity Low; the action that closes it is an issuer statement of unadjusted EBITDA, which the filings do not give.

The fourth quarter of 2025 is not printed as a separate quarter and no fourth-quarter release is supplied, so its revenue and EBITDA are derived as the year less nine months and nothing else is stated for it. Severity Low; the action is to obtain the fourth-quarter 2025 release if discrete-quarter work is needed.

Several lines are not presented in the 2026 interim statements (loss on early extinguishment of debt, gain on sale of businesses, deferred income taxes, proceeds from sale of businesses, proceeds from issuance of debt and payment on the revolving facility) and some print a dash for a period; they are marked not supplied rather than zero. Severity Low; the figures that depend on them, such as nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, reconcile without them.

Carrying values are not disclosed for each debt instrument, only an aggregate of unamortized issuance costs of USD 25,652 thousand at September 30, 2026, so the debt instruments table carries principal and one financing cost adjustment. Severity Low; the action is an instrument-level carrying value, which the filings do not give.

The latest maturity ladder printed is at December 31, 2025 and there is none at September 30, 2026, so the maturity chart omits the 2034 notes of October 2026 and the revolver borrowing outstanding at the quarter end. Severity Medium; the action is to rebuild the ladder from the next annual report or the executed documents.

The pro forma net debt rests on principal amounts: the net proceeds and issuance costs of the 2034 notes are not stated, and the issuer expects EnviroServe to add about USD 27 million of Adjusted EBITDA a year but has not reported any, so pro forma net leverage excludes the acquired earnings and may differ by the unstated costs. Severity Medium; the action is the issuer statement of net proceeds and the first reported EnviroServe results in a later filing.

Finance lease liabilities of USD 229,317 thousand at December 31, 2025 and USD 186,705 thousand at December 31, 2024 sit inside accrued and other long-term liabilities, outside total debt, and no finance lease balance is printed at September 30, 2026, so a lease-adjusted leverage figure cannot be stated for the latest date. Severity Medium; the action is the finance lease balance from the next annual report.

The issuer says its loan covenants are based on levels of Adjusted EBITDA but prints no covenant level, test date or definition, and the executed debt documents are not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculable and is not inferred. Severity Medium; the action is to obtain the executed credit agreements and indentures.

Cash interest paid over the last twelve months is affected by coupon dates that moved with the October 2025 refinancing, so the interest cover for that period is not a steady-state figure. Severity Medium; the action is to compare it with the accrued interest expense in the next annual report.

The order of the revolving facility against the term loans is not stated in the filings, which describe the revolver as secured on receivables and the term loans as secured on substantially all assets, so the debt stack shows both secured facilities at the first rank; the notes of 2029, 2031 and 2033 are shown at one rank because the filings do not say pari passu. Severity Low; the action is the intercreditor agreement, which is not supplied.

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: Evidence for the view is also strong: no dividend has ever been paid, repurchases come from cash and can stop, covenant compliance and effective internal control are reported, and the 2025 refinancing extended maturities without adding secured debt to the notes. facts.label: Business profile, ownership and group structure
facts.text: Clean Harbors collects, treats, recycles and disposes of hazardous and non-hazardous waste across North America through permitted incinerators, landfills and treatment sites and re-refines used oil; Environmental Services supplies 83.44% of nine-month 2026 revenue and the oil segment 16.56%. The issuer describes its permits as hard to replicate and customers keep generator liability, so established vendors hold recurring volumes, which supports cash-flow visibility and debt service. Ownership is dispersed with no sponsor or controlling holder named, so creditor protection rests on board and management policy, and the proxy statement that would show holdings and independence is not supplied. The notes are guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries and rank behind secured debt and non-guarantor subsidiaries, and Canada, at 8.56% of revenue, sits outside the note guarantee as the debt note words it. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_clh.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_clh.htm.jsonl, page 137; calculation C17

facts.label: Revenue durability and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is mostly recurring and generator-driven, with cyclical and non-scheduled parts. Technical Services and the Safety-Kleen core services follow industrial volumes and pricing, Field and Emergency Response varies with events, and Safety-Kleen Oil follows product prices, with revenue down 15.10% in 2025 and up 26.70% in nine months 2026; emergency response and oil together are 28.93% of nine-month revenue. Customers face a financial burden in switching hazardous waste vendors, which supports pricing, and the ten-year disposal contract adds visibility at USD 60.0 million a year, 0.99% of 2025 revenue, so the core is durable but the 2026 growth rate is not a run rate. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Costs are labour, equipment, fuel and transport on top of the fixed cost of permitted assets, and the issuer passes much of the inflation through pricing and fuel surcharges. In Q3 2026 Environmental Services cost of revenues rose 16.4% against revenue growth of 16.5%, with labour and benefits up USD 75.0 million, equipment and supplies up USD 33.2 million and fuel and transport up USD 31.3 million, yet the segment margin held at 27.4% against 26.8%. Margins can be defended at current volumes; under volume pressure the fixed cost of ten incinerators and seven landfills would deleverage margins, and the oil segment margin depends on product spreads that the issuer does not control. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is real but split by service: national firms such as Veolia North America, Enviri, Republic Services, Waste Management, GFL Environmental and Crystal Clean compete in parts of the offer and hundreds of private firms compete locally, while the issuer states no one competitor offers its full range, which limits price competition in the integrated disposal business. New entry is constrained by permitting, regulatory approval and capital cost of incinerators and landfills. Substitutes such as in-house disposal are limited because regulatory requirements can make captive disposal too capital intensive or complex, and the issuer lists market incineration capacity, including captive incineration closures, among the factors that drive revenue. Buyer power is low by concentration, with no customer above 10% of revenue, and generator liability makes customers cautious about switching, while supplier power sits mainly in fuel, labour and used-oil feedstock, where fuel and transport cost rose USD 31.3 million in Q3 2026 and was passed through. facts.label: Regulatory and macroeconomic factors
facts.text: Regulation and the industrial cycle both matter to credit. PFAS regulation drives demand for filtration, remediation and disposal, and a PFAS project added over USD 40 million of revenue in nine months 2026; the issuer also cites improving US manufacturing activity, reshoring and data center work as demand support, and lists tariffs and new legislation among its risks. The same rules raise compliance and closure costs, with closure, post-closure and remedial liabilities of USD 232,686 thousand, so regulation supports volumes and prices while adding long-dated cash obligations; floating-rate debt adds an interest-rate factor. facts.text: On the nine dimensions the issuer assesses as follows. Scale and market position are strong, and competitive advantage is strong on permits and utilization. The trend is rising earnings and rising debt; the missing datapoints are ratings, covenant levels and the proxy statement. facts.text: In the next 12 to 24 months the issuer guides fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA growth of 23% to 26%, full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1.44 billion to USD 1.48 billion and adjusted free cash flow of USD 600 million to USD 660 million, with the ten-year contract started in Q4 and the PFAS pipeline described as robust; these support revenue and deleveraging if debt stops rising. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The downside begins with oil product prices easing as supply disruption ends while the large emergency response and PFAS projects fade. The first break is the oil segment margin falling towards 16.8%, which in the illustration removes the USD 144,954 thousand nine-month increase and lowers last-twelve-month reported EBITDA to USD 1,179,694 thousand. Financial transmission is pro forma net leverage of 2.49x instead of 2.22x, with cash interest cover lower because the 2034 notes add USD 37.5 million a year and the swaps end on 2027-09-30. Liquidity of USD 759,044 thousand still covers USD 37.8 million of scheduled principal for 2026 to 2028 at the end of 2025, so distress is not indicated; management can stop repurchases of USD 75.0 million, cut strategic growth investment of USD 145 million and pause acquisitions, and the observable triggers are the oil segment margin, pro forma leverage and the 2029 refinancing plan. Covenant headroom cannot be measured, so the scenario tests liquidity and leverage only. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C06; calculation C09; calculation C13; calculation C16

Liquidity of USD 759,044 thousand still covers USD 37.8 million of scheduled principal for 2026 to 2028 at the end of 2025, so distress is not indicated; management can stop repurchases of USD 75.0 million, cut strategic growth investment of USD 145 million and pause acquisitions, and the observable triggers are the oil segment margin, pro forma leverage and the 2029 refinancing plan. Covenant headroom cannot be measured, so the scenario tests liquidity and leverage only.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C06; calculation C09; calculation C13; calculation C16

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Clean Harbors presents a strong business profile supported by permit-protected assets, customer spread and liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by debt-assisted acquisitions and earnings that lean on oil prices. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow is 37.79% of reported EBITDA and 2026 growth spending absorbed it. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on delivering synergies and holding leverage near the 2.22x pro forma level before the 2029 maturities and the swap expiry on 2027-09-30. The primary downside path is an oil price reversal with fading project revenue on a higher debt base. Further analysis would require ratings, covenant levels, the proxy statement and the reported earnings of the acquired businesses. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: debt-assisted acquisitions lifting leverage while oil-driven earnings can reverse. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C13; calculation C15

## Findings
### Bottom line

The eleven supplied files support a credit snapshot of Clean Harbors Inc through the quarter ended September 30, 2026, but not covenant, legal-priority, ratings or market-pricing conclusions, so creditors should treat those areas as unevidenced.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4, 16–19; calculation C1

Both annual reports, the three 2026 quarterly reports and six press releases give audited annual and unaudited quarterly statements from 2024 to September 30, 2026, and the newest source is dated 21 days before the 2026-11-18 cutoff. The 2034 unsecured notes of USD 600 million issued on October 1, 2026 and the EnviroServe acquisition of about USD 470 million completed on October 2, 2026 appear only as post-quarter disclosures, so quarter-end debt, cash and leverage exclude them and no pro forma figure is printed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 18–19; calculation C3

No debt ratings, executed indentures or credit agreements, market quotes, peer set or portfolio data were supplied, and the proxy statement that holds board and compensation detail is absent, so covenant and governance findings can rest only on filing summaries.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Clean Harbors carries moderate leverage, with net debt at 1.86x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at September 30, 2026, but the October 2026 EnviroServe purchase lifts that to 2.22x pro forma before any earnings from the target, so creditors should anchor on the higher figure.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 16–19; calculation C22; calculation C08; calculation C30

Gross leverage fell from 2.49x at the end of 2025 to 2.18x as last-twelve-months EBITDA grew faster than debt, and cash interest paid is covered 9.61x, but the gain leans on high re-refined product prices and one emergency response event worth about USD 120 million of revenue, either of which can reverse.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 16–19; EX99.1_2026-09-30_clh_clh-q32026pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation C17; calculation C08; calculation C10
The issuer states only adjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is derived from the statements; on the issuer's adjusted measure net leverage is 1.77x, or 2.11x pro forma.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_clh.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 42; calculation C36; calculation C30
### Leverage and coverage

Net leverage on reported EBITDA moved from 1.96x at the end of 2024 to 1.75x at the end of 2025 and 1.86x on the twelve months to September 30, 2026, while gross leverage moved from 2.61x to 2.49x and 2.18x. Earnings growth lowered gross leverage in 2026, but net leverage rose because USD 689,044 thousand of acquisitions and USD 77,133 thousand of share repurchases helped cut cash by USD 402,771 thousand over nine months; the October 2026 purchase was then financed from the proceeds of new notes rather than from cash on hand.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4; calculation C19; calculation C22; calculation C08

Cash interest paid of USD 137,780 thousand over the last twelve months is covered 9.61x by reported EBITDA against 7.10x for 2025. The comparison flatters the latest cover because coupon dates moved with the October 2025 refinancing, and the issuer guides 2026 interest expense, net of interest income, of USD 155 million to USD 160 million, which is above the cash interest paid in the latest twelve months even before interest income is added back.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_clh_clh-q32026pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_clh.htm.jsonl, page 135; calculation C10
### Cash flow quality

Operating cash flow of USD 664,673 thousand for nine months 2026, against USD 511,632 thousand a year earlier, funded capital spending of USD 397,480 thousand, but a USD 276,946 thousand build in receivables as revenue grew absorbed part of it. The issuer's adjusted free cash flow of USD 382,981 thousand is higher than operating cash flow less capital spending by USD 115,788 thousand because the issuer adds back USD 107,305 thousand of strategic growth investment and USD 8,483 thousand of asset sale proceeds.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX99.1_2026-09-30_clh_clh-q32026pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C40
### Liquidity and maturities

Cash and cash equivalents were USD 423,544 thousand at September 30, 2026, with a further USD 93,010 thousand of short-term marketable securities, and USD 335.5 million was available under the USD 600.0 million revolving facility after a USD 120.0 million borrowing and USD 144.5 million of letters of credit. Apart from term loan amortization of USD 12.6 million a year, the earliest scheduled maturity is the 2029 notes, so scheduled refinancing needs before 2029 are limited to that amortization; the revolver borrowing was repaid in October 2026 and the facility runs to June 2029.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 18, 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_clh.htm.jsonl, pages 95, 138; calculation C26
### Subsequent events and pro forma net debt

After the balance sheet date the issuer sold USD 600.0 million of 2034 unsecured senior notes on October 1, 2026, paid about USD 470 million in cash for EnviroServe on October 2, 2026 and repaid the USD 120.0 million revolver borrowing on October 16, 2026. These events are kept out of the period figures; they raise net debt by about USD 470 million and put pro forma net leverage at 2.22x on reported EBITDA and 2.11x on adjusted EBITDA, before any earnings from EnviroServe, which the issuer expects to be about USD 27 million of Adjusted EBITDA a year before cost synergies.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 18–19; EX99.1_2026-06-30_clh_enviroservepressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C28; calculation C30
### Data quality and definitions

Reported EBITDA is derived because the issuer states none, and the issuer says its loan covenants are based on Adjusted EBITDA without printing a covenant level, so no headroom can be stated. Finance lease liabilities of USD 229,317 thousand at the end of 2025 sit outside total debt and would raise gross leverage from 2.49x to 2.69x; the definition register and the gaps below list the other limits.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_clh.htm.jsonl, pages 75, 150; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 42; calculation C38
### Chart data: leverage

## Gaps

The issuer states only Adjusted EBITDA and no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is derived from net income, income taxes, net interest and depreciation and amortization; every leverage and cover figure depends on that derivation, and the issuer-adjusted ratios are shown beside each one. Severity Low; the action that closes it is an issuer statement of unadjusted EBITDA, which the filings do not give.

The fourth quarter of 2025 is not printed as a separate quarter and no fourth-quarter release is supplied, so its revenue and EBITDA are derived as the year less nine months and nothing else is stated for it. Severity Low; the action is to obtain the fourth-quarter 2025 release if discrete-quarter work is needed.

Several lines are not presented in the 2026 interim statements (loss on early extinguishment of debt, gain on sale of businesses, deferred income taxes, proceeds from sale of businesses, proceeds from issuance of debt and payment on the revolving facility) and some print a dash for a period; they are marked not supplied rather than zero. Severity Low; the figures that depend on them, such as nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, reconcile without them.

Carrying values are not disclosed for each debt instrument, only an aggregate of unamortized issuance costs of USD 25,652 thousand at September 30, 2026, so the debt instruments table carries principal and one financing cost adjustment. Severity Low; the action is an instrument-level carrying value, which the filings do not give.

The latest maturity ladder printed is at December 31, 2025 and there is none at September 30, 2026, so the maturity chart omits the 2034 notes of October 2026 and the revolver borrowing outstanding at the quarter end. Severity Medium; the action is to rebuild the ladder from the next annual report or the executed documents.

The pro forma net debt rests on principal amounts: the net proceeds and issuance costs of the 2034 notes are not stated, and the issuer expects EnviroServe to add about USD 27 million of Adjusted EBITDA a year but has not reported any, so pro forma net leverage excludes the acquired earnings and may differ by the unstated costs. Severity Medium; the action is the issuer statement of net proceeds and the first reported EnviroServe results in a later filing.

Finance lease liabilities of USD 229,317 thousand at December 31, 2025 and USD 186,705 thousand at December 31, 2024 sit inside accrued and other long-term liabilities, outside total debt, and no finance lease balance is printed at September 30, 2026, so a lease-adjusted leverage figure cannot be stated for the latest date. Severity Medium; the action is the finance lease balance from the next annual report.

The issuer says its loan covenants are based on levels of Adjusted EBITDA but prints no covenant level, test date or definition, and the executed debt documents are not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculable and is not inferred. Severity Medium; the action is to obtain the executed credit agreements and indentures.

Cash interest paid over the last twelve months is affected by coupon dates that moved with the October 2025 refinancing, so the interest cover for that period is not a steady-state figure. Severity Medium; the action is to compare it with the accrued interest expense in the next annual report.

The order of the revolving facility against the term loans is not stated in the filings, which describe the revolver as secured on receivables and the term loans as secured on substantially all assets, so the debt stack shows both secured facilities at the first rank; the notes of 2029, 2031 and 2033 are shown at one rank because the filings do not say pari passu. Severity Low; the action is the intercreditor agreement, which is not supplied.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Clean Harbors is a widely held public company with no controlling shareholder or sponsor named in the filings, so creditors depend on management and board discipline rather than owner support, and 2026 shows debt-assisted acquisitions running beside continued share repurchases.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_clh.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 48; calculation C09

The business is a North American hazardous-waste and used-oil network. Environmental Services supplies 83.44% of nine-month 2026 revenue, while the oil segment margin rose to 31.4% on product prices that can reverse. Five 2026 purchases total USD 1,158.0 million, the largest, EnviroServe at USD 470 million, paid from new notes, and the proxy statement that would show board independence and holdings is not supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C01; calculation C09
### Key findings

No controlling holder or sponsor is identified, so the question for creditors is the discipline of the board and management, not owner behaviour. The annual report counts about two hundred holders of record and well over one hundred thousand beneficial holders, gives no holder percentage, and leaves ownership, independence and committee detail to a proxy statement that is not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_clh.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-K_2025-12-31_clh.htm.jsonl, page 159

Business risk is diversified by customer and service line but concentrated in capital-intensive disposal assets. No customer exceeded 10% of revenue, the top ten industries supplied about 80% of 2025 revenue and no service line exceeded 29.64% of nine-month 2026 revenue, but ten incinerators and seven landfills carry fixed costs, so margins depend on keeping throughput high.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_clh.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_clh.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_clh.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C04; calculation C19

Earnings are moving toward the price-driven oil segment, so part of the 2026 improvement should be treated as cyclical. The segment margin was 31.4% in nine months 2026 against 16.8% a year earlier and its share of segment Adjusted EBITDA rose from 9.64% to 18.37%, but oil product revenue fell 15.10% in 2025 before rising 26.70% in 2026 and the issuer ties the strength to global shortages; the larger Environmental Services margin was steadier at 26.3% against 25.9%.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_clh.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2025-12-31_clh.htm.jsonl, pages 67–68; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35; EX99.1_2026-09-30_clh_clh-q32026pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C08

Acquisitions are now a repeated, debt-assisted strategy priced richly before synergies, so creditors rely on synergy delivery that the filings do not evidence. Five 2026 purchases total USD 1,158.0 million, the issuer counts five transactions this year as part of its growth strategy and USD 500.0 million of term loans funded the 2024 deals; the issuer expectations imply 15.00x for Terra Nova and 17.41x for EnviroServe before synergies against 11.84x and 9.04x after, and pro forma effects of the four completed deals are called immaterial.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, pages 11–14; EX99.1_2026-09-30_clh_clh-q32026pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_clh.htm.jsonl, page 135; EX99.1_2026-03-31_clh_terranovapressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-06-30_clh_enviroservepressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C09; calculation C11

Shareholder returns are limited to discretionary repurchases funded from cash, which supports creditors but does not bind the board. The company has never paid a dividend, debt documents limit dividends and repurchases, and USD 75.0 million of repurchases in nine months 2026 follow USD 249.8 million in 2025, with USD 524.4 million of authority left that the Board can stop at any time.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_clh.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-K_2025-12-31_clh.htm.jsonl, page 143; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation C14; calculation C15

Governance structure is visible but cannot be tested. Thirteen directors signed the annual report, three of them executives, a lead independent director exists, the audit and internal control opinions are clean and no related-party leakage is evidenced, and equity awards vest on revenue, Adjusted EBITDA, margin, return on invested capital and safety measures with no debt measure named, but independence of the other ten directors, committee membership and holdings sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against reading Clean Harbors as a disciplined public-company borrower is the pace of 2026: five purchases in nine months for USD 1,158.0 million, the last paid with new notes at an expected 17.41x before synergies, alongside USD 75.0 million of repurchases. If debt-funded purchasing continues into 2027, or if the USD 25 million and USD 4 million of expected synergies are not delivered, creditors would be financing a roll-up whose returns rest on issuer estimates.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, pages 11–14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 48; EX99.1_2026-06-30_clh_enviroservepressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-03-31_clh_terranovapressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C09; calculation C11

Evidence for the view is also strong: no dividend has ever been paid, repurchases come from cash and can stop, covenant compliance and effective internal control are reported, and the 2025 refinancing extended maturities without adding secured debt to the notes. The view would turn to a higher-risk reading if the proxy statement showed a holder with board seats or veto rights, if no independent Chair is appointed, if the debt documents allowed large restricted payments, or if acquired earnings fall short of the issuer expectations of USD 27 million and USD 15 million; it would turn to a lower-risk reading if an independent Chair is confirmed, covenant levels show wide headroom and the 2026 purchases are integrated without further debt-funded deals.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Clean Harbors is a moderately leveraged, permit-protected waste network whose credit quality is constrained by debt-assisted acquisitions, which lift net leverage from 1.86x at 2026-09-30 to 2.22x pro forma after the 2026-10-02 EnviroServe purchase, and by earnings that lean on oil prices.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C14

Liquidity gives time: USD 759,044 thousand of cash and undrawn revolver at 2026-09-30, with pro forma cash not established, and no note due before 2029. The primary downside path is lower oil product prices and fewer one-off projects while integration costs and interest rise, so creditors should watch pro forma leverage and the oil segment margin.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_clh.htm.jsonl, page 133; calculation C06; calculation C15
### Key findings

The overall profile is adequate to strong on business quality and liquidity and weakest on financial policy, because debt-assisted acquisitions are lifting leverage faster than reported earnings can show. Net leverage was 1.86x at 2026-09-30 and 2.22x pro forma after the 2026-10-02 EnviroServe purchase, or 1.77x and 2.11x on adjusted EBITDA, and pro forma net debt is 50.59% above the end of 2025 while last-twelve-month reported EBITDA is 18.58% higher.

### Business profile, ownership and group structure

Clean Harbors collects, treats, recycles and disposes of hazardous and non-hazardous waste across North America through permitted incinerators, landfills and treatment sites and re-refines used oil; Environmental Services supplies 83.44% of nine-month 2026 revenue and the oil segment 16.56%. The issuer describes its permits as hard to replicate and customers keep generator liability, so established vendors hold recurring volumes, which supports cash-flow visibility and debt service. Ownership is dispersed with no sponsor or controlling holder named, so creditor protection rests on board and management policy, and the proxy statement that would show holdings and independence is not supplied. The notes are guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries and rank behind secured debt and non-guarantor subsidiaries, and Canada, at 8.56% of revenue, sits outside the note guarantee as the debt note words it.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_clh.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_clh.htm.jsonl, page 137; calculation C17
### Revenue durability and pricing power

Revenue is mostly recurring and generator-driven, with cyclical and non-scheduled parts. Technical Services and the Safety-Kleen core services follow industrial volumes and pricing, Field and Emergency Response varies with events, and Safety-Kleen Oil follows product prices, with revenue down 15.10% in 2025 and up 26.70% in nine months 2026; emergency response and oil together are 28.93% of nine-month revenue. Customers face a financial burden in switching hazardous waste vendors, which supports pricing, and the ten-year disposal contract adds visibility at USD 60.0 million a year, 0.99% of 2025 revenue, so the core is durable but the 2026 growth rate is not a run rate.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_clh.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C18
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Costs are labour, equipment, fuel and transport on top of the fixed cost of permitted assets, and the issuer passes much of the inflation through pricing and fuel surcharges. In Q3 2026 Environmental Services cost of revenues rose 16.4% against revenue growth of 16.5%, with labour and benefits up USD 75.0 million, equipment and supplies up USD 33.2 million and fuel and transport up USD 31.3 million, yet the segment margin held at 27.4% against 26.8%. Margins can be defended at current volumes; under volume pressure the fixed cost of ten incinerators and seven landfills would deleverage margins, and the oil segment margin depends on product spreads that the issuer does not control.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 38
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Cash conversion is moderate and flexible at the growth end. Capital spending was 39.20% of last-twelve-month reported EBITDA and free cash flow 37.79%, receivables and unbilled receivables rose as revenue grew, and the 2026 guidance includes USD 145 million of strategic growth investment that the issuer adds back to adjusted free cash flow. Because that growth spending and the USD 75.0 million of repurchases are discretionary, free cash flow can be redirected to debt reduction if acquisitions pause, which is the main lever behind the deleveraging case.

### Competitive forces

Rivalry is real but split by service: national firms such as Veolia North America, Enviri, Republic Services, Waste Management, GFL Environmental and Crystal Clean compete in parts of the offer and hundreds of private firms compete locally, while the issuer states no one competitor offers its full range, which limits price competition in the integrated disposal business. New entry is constrained by permitting, regulatory approval and capital cost of incinerators and landfills. Substitutes such as in-house disposal are limited because regulatory requirements can make captive disposal too capital intensive or complex, and the issuer lists market incineration capacity, including captive incineration closures, among the factors that drive revenue. Buyer power is low by concentration, with no customer above 10% of revenue, and generator liability makes customers cautious about switching, while supplier power sits mainly in fuel, labour and used-oil feedstock, where fuel and transport cost rose USD 31.3 million in Q3 2026 and was passed through.

Regulation and the industrial cycle both matter to credit. PFAS regulation drives demand for filtration, remediation and disposal, and a PFAS project added over USD 40 million of revenue in nine months 2026; the issuer also cites improving US manufacturing activity, reshoring and data center work as demand support, and lists tariffs and new legislation among its risks. Strengths are the permitted network, customer spread, rising core margin and liquidity of USD 759,044 thousand. ### Financial profile and credit quality

On the nine dimensions the issuer assesses as follows. Scale and market position are strong, and competitive advantage is strong on permits and utilization. Business diversification is average, because customers and industries are spread but 83.44% of revenue is one segment. Cost and capex flexibility is average, with fixed-cost assets offset by discretionary growth spending, and margin stability is average, because the core margin is steady and the oil margin is not. Free cash flow stability is average at 37.79% of reported EBITDA, ability to refinance is strong on completed issues and the maturity profile, liquidity is strong at USD 759,044 thousand against USD 37.8 million of scheduled principal for 2026 to 2028 at the end of 2025, and financial policy and governance is average and the weakest on evidence. The trend is rising earnings and rising debt; the missing datapoints are ratings, covenant levels and the proxy statement.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

In the next 12 to 24 months the issuer guides fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA growth of 23% to 26%, full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1.44 billion to USD 1.48 billion and adjusted free cash flow of USD 600 million to USD 660 million, with the ten-year contract started in Q4 and the PFAS pipeline described as robust; these support revenue and deleveraging if debt stops rising. Headwinds are oil price normalisation, fewer events, higher interest and integration cost, with integration and strategic project costs already USD 13.5 million in nine months 2026. Over three to five years the issuer points to reshoring, PFAS regulation and captive incineration closures as demand drivers, but the supplied filings give no forecast beyond 2026.

### Downside scenario

The downside begins with oil product prices easing as supply disruption ends while the large emergency response and PFAS projects fade. The first break is the oil segment margin falling towards 16.8%, which in the illustration removes the USD 144,954 thousand nine-month increase and lowers last-twelve-month reported EBITDA to USD 1,179,694 thousand. Financial transmission is pro forma net leverage of 2.49x instead of 2.22x, with cash interest cover lower because the 2034 notes add USD 37.5 million a year and the swaps end on 2027-09-30. Liquidity of USD 759,044 thousand still covers USD 37.8 million of scheduled principal for 2026 to 2028 at the end of 2025, so distress is not indicated; management can stop repurchases of USD 75.0 million, cut strategic growth investment of USD 145 million and pause acquisitions, and the observable triggers are the oil segment margin, pro forma leverage and the 2029 refinancing plan. Covenant headroom cannot be measured, so the scenario tests liquidity and leverage only.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clh.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C06; calculation C09; calculation C13; calculation C16
### Overall credit view

Overall, Clean Harbors presents a strong business profile supported by permit-protected assets, customer spread and liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by debt-assisted acquisitions and earnings that lean on oil prices. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow is 37.79% of reported EBITDA and 2026 growth spending absorbed it. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on delivering synergies and holding leverage near the 2.22x pro forma level before the 2029 maturities and the swap expiry on 2027-09-30. The primary downside path is an oil price reversal with fading project revenue on a higher debt base. Further analysis would require ratings, covenant levels, the proxy statement and the reported earnings of the acquired businesses. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: debt-assisted acquisitions lifting leverage while oil-driven earnings can reverse.
